newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - MAY 30.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - President Vaclav Havel has apprehension and "doubts" about the cabinet's stabilisation programme. He announced yesterday after meeting with coalition leaders that for the moment, however, he will support it, giving the cabinet a chance to fix "mistakes caused by the cabinet's policy up to now".

- There has been a buying fever in the past few days in domestic stores. In reaction to the cabinet's measures, people have mostly bought non-food items, primarily electrical appliances, refrigerators and furniture. Some retailers have begun increasing prices, even though they have not sold out of their supplies.
- The crown strengthened yesterday to up to 18.85 to the mark. Most dealers claim this is due to the high level of interest rates. Volumes were low, however.

- After a decline in the first three months of this year by 1.5 percent, industrial sales increased year-on-year by 10.1 percent in April, according to preliminary reports from the Czech Statistical Bureau.
- Since the beginning of the year, Chemopetrol a.s. has had revenue of 5.8 billion crowns and profits before taxes of 465 million crowns, which is more than half of its planned profit for the year.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - Deputy Prime Minister Josef Lux said yesterday that his party, KDU-CSL, believes that no coalition-party chairmen, himself included, should be present in the cabinet.

- Relations with the EU are still tarnished with the import deposit that the cabinet introduced due to the high trade deficit. Meetings in Brussels with representatives of the Czech Republic did not lead to an agreement, and another meeting will be held at the end of June.
- Holding Kladno, through which the state holds a minority stake in Poldi Steel, is bankrupt, following the bankruptcy of Poldi Steel itself and Bohemia Art, the majority shareholder.

- A constitutional court in Brno ruled yesterday that the fine of 3.5 million crowns, which Skoda Automobilova was issued from the former Antitrust Office due to misuse of its dominant position on the market.

PRAVO - Benzina a.s. will increase its Special petrol and motor oil at its network of service stations by 50 hellers per litre from June 1. Natural and super will increase by 60 hellers per litre, in reaction to price increases at Ceska Rafinerska.

- During a meeting today of the opposition Social Democrats (CSSD), the party's leader and Parliamentary Chairman Milos Zeman plans to propose that CSSD issue a proclamation that the cabinet is untrustworthy.
- Prices for imported Seat vehicles are increasing by 10 percent, effective immediately. A possible increase in Audi and Volkswagen prices will be announced at the beginning of next week.
- According to the chairman of the National Property Fund, Roman Ceska, all stakes of non-strategic companies worth 30 billion crowns will be privatised by the end of this year.

LIDOVE NOVINY - From June 2, Ceska Sporitelna is changing its timed-account rates on deposit books and credits for physical persons. Interest for physical persons will increase to 16 percent and to 19 percent for legal persons.

- The billboard for the energy drink Erectus, which depicts the Pope covering his eyes to a long pair of legs exposed by a strong gust of wind and the slogan, "When you want more than you can," violates the ethics code for advertising, according to the Advertising Council.

- Labour and Social Affairs Minister Jindrich Vodicka does not expect that approval of valorisation of pensions, social security of compensation for increasing energy prices will be stopped this year.
- Investicni a Postovni Banka plans to increase fixed yearly interest rates by up to 22.2 percentage points for weekly accounts and by five points for credits as of June 2.
- Zapadoceska Plynarenska Spolecnost will not pay dividends for 1996, on profits of 84 million crowns. The company will reinvest its net profits of 41 million crowns.
